I was up all night organizing old lesson plans, starting new projects, calling former colleagues just to share “brilliant ideas.” I felt high, almost giddy, but then I’d snap into anger if my husband asked me to slow down. But that only lasted about two weeks—then that energy just vanished, and I crashed.

Since then, I can’t feel anything. No joy in my garden, no comfort seeing friends—nothing. I pace constantly, can’t sit through a meal. My mind’s been playing tricks on me, though. There’s this voice, sometimes whispering, sometimes clear, saying things like “they know what you did,” and I know people are talking about me in code—on the bus, even my daughter’s laughter sounds directed at me. That doesn’t go away, even now when I’m not feeling manic anymore. The thoughts come and go: “I want to die,” though I wouldn’t act on it. But the voices and those suspicious feelings? They’ve stuck around long after that burst of energy faded.
